Chapter Two: Clarifying Intentions and Setting Meaningful Goals
So, once you’ve gotten clear on your own self-awareness, what comes next? Well, now it’s about figuring out exactly what you want to change— and, maybe even more importantly, why it matters to you.
If you’ve ever made a vague wish for things to be different, you probably know how quickly that fades. But once you set a clear intention and a specific goal? Suddenly, you’ve got real direction— and the motivation to actually move forward.
Now, setting an intention isn’t just about picking a new habit to start, or an old one to give up. It’s about tying that change to something deeper— your values, your hopes, maybe even your vision for your future. Let’s say you want to eat healthier. Sure, you could just say, “Yeah, I want to eat better.” But what if you connect it to wanting more energy, more confidence, or a longer, healthier life? Suddenly, that intention carries real weight.
Here’s something that really helps: visualize the outcome. Imagine yourself already living with this habit in place. How does it feel? What’s different about your day? Thinking it through like this not only makes your goal clearer, but it also makes it feel real— and way more exciting to chase.
When you’re setting goals, there are a few things to keep in mind:
First, make it specific. Don’t settle for “exercise more.” Try something like, “I’ll walk for 30 minutes every morning.” The clearer you are, the easier it is to follow through.
Next, make sure it’s measurable. Pick goals you can actually track, so you can see your progress and celebrate those little wins along the way.
And make it relevant. Ask yourself, does this habit line up with what really matters to me? Is it moving me toward the life I want?
Finally, keep it achievable. It’s great to aim high, but if you set the bar too high, it can feel overwhelming. Steady progress wins the race.
Picture someone who wants to read more books. Instead of just hoping they’ll read more, they decide to read ten pages every night before bed. That’s clear, it’s measurable, and it’s easy to fit into a routine.
There will be days when motivation dips— that’s normal. But if you’ve anchored your goal to a deeper “why,” you’ll have something to lean on when things get tough. Maybe you remember that regular exercise helps you manage stress and feel stronger— and that’s enough to get you moving on the days you’d rather not.
Here’s a tip: Write your intentions down, and put them somewhere you’ll see them often. Even a short statement, like, “I move my body every morning to feel energized and clear-headed,” can be a powerful reminder. Stick it on your mirror, your desk, or even your phone— wherever it’ll catch your eye.
So, let’s sum up a few strategies for clarifying intentions and setting goals:
Visualize success— really picture how your life will feel with this new habit.
Write a purpose statement. Just a sentence or two that sums up what you want and why it matters.
And break your big goals into small, daily actions that feel doable.
When your habits are anchored in clear intentions and meaningful goals, the path forward is a whole lot clearer— and you’ll have the resilience to stick with it, even when life throws you a curveball. That clarity doesn’t just guide your choices day by day— it also keeps you motivated when things get tough.
